origin.description: Locate every run of code points that belong to a character class.
origin.usage: stri_locate_all_charclass(str, pattern, merge = TRUE, omit_no_match = FALSE, get_length = FALSE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

arguments.name: merge
arguments.text: If TRUE, join consecutive matching code points into one row.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If TRUE, a miss contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: If TRUE, the second column is the length in code points. A miss is then -1, -1.

origin.details: Indexes are 1-based and inclusive. A missing string or pattern is one NA, NA row even when get_length is TRUE. An empty string with get_length is -1, -1.
origin.value: A list of two-column integer matrices.
origin.example:
x <- stri_locate_all_charclass("a1b", "\\p{N}")[[1]]
sentence <- paste0('stri_locate_all_charclass("a1b", "\\p{N}") returns ', paste(x, collapse = ", "), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Locate every run of code points that belong to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

arguments.name: merge
arguments.text: If true, join consecutive matching code points into one row.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If true, a miss contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: If true, the second column is the length in code points. A miss is then -1, -1.

translation.details: Indexes are 1-based and inclusive. A missing string or pattern is one NA, NA row even when get_length is true. An empty string with get_length is -1, -1.
translation.value: A list of matrices. Each matrix is a list of [start, end] rows.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_locate_all_charclass
x = stri_locate_all_charclass("a1b", "\\p{N}")
sentence = f'stri_locate_all_charclass("a1b", "\\p{{N}}") returns {x[0][0][0]}, {x[0][0][1]}.'
print(sentence)
